title: 'The Interview': Robert Putnam Knows Why You’re Lonely

sentences.zh: 七十年的太空探索。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.

sentences.en: From The New York Times, this is The Interview.
sentences.zh: 这里是《纽约时报》的《访谈》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia Navarro.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚·纳瓦罗。

sentences.en: This isn't going to come as a newsflash.
sentences.zh: 这算不上什么新闻快讯。

sentences.en: Things feel fragile in America.
sentences.zh: 在美国，一切都显得脆弱不堪。

sentences.en: And there is a broad consensus across parties and demographics that we are struggling to come together and face our many challenges.
sentences.zh: 各党派和各阶层之间存在广泛共识，即我们正艰难地团结起来，共同面对诸多挑战。

sentences.en: Which is why, when I heard about a new documentary about the Harvard political scientist Robert Putnam, I knew I wanted to talk to him.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，当我听说有一部关于哈佛政治学家罗伯特·普特南的新纪录片时，我就知道我想和他谈谈。

sentences.en: Nearly three decades ago, Putnam became something pretty rare.
sentences.zh: 近三十年前，普特南成了一个相当罕见的人物。

sentences.en: A celebrity academic.
sentences.zh: 一位明星学者。

sentences.en: In 1995, he published a groundbreaking paper called
sentences.zh: 1995年，他发表了一篇开创性的论文，题为

sentences.en: Bowling Alone, America's Declining Social Capital.
sentences.zh: 《独自打保龄：美国社会资本的衰落》。

sentences.en: In it, he used data from the previous few decades to prove that America was transforming from a nation of joiners to a nation of loners.
sentences.zh: 在文中，他利用过去几十年的数据证明，美国正从一个“参与者之国”转变为一个“孤独者之国”。

sentences.en: We were going to church less, joining clubs at declining rates.
sentences.zh: 我们去教堂的次数减少了，加入俱乐部的比例也在下降。

sentences.en: And he warned that as a result, we were losing trust in our fellow Americans and our institutions.
sentences.zh: 他警告说，结果就是我们正在失去对同胞和机构的信任。

sentences.en: That paper caught the attention of then-President Bill Clinton.
sentences.zh: 那篇论文引起了时任总统比尔·克林顿的注意。

sentences.en: And before long, regular people couldn't stop talking about it either.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，普通民众也开始热议此事。

sentences.en: However, Putnam expanded it into a best-selling book a few years later.
sentences.zh: 然而，几年后普特南将其扩展成了一本畅销书。

sentences.en: And for a moment, it seemed like his work might pull us back from this isolation highway we were all on.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，似乎他的著作能让我们从这条孤独的道路上回头。

sentences.en: We all know how that story unfolded.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道后来发生了什么。

sentences.en: Putnam's now 83.
sentences.zh: 普特南现在83岁了。

sentences.en: And he's watched as we've become more divided, more lonely, and less confident about the way forward than ever before, even as the stakes only get higher.
sentences.zh: 他眼看着我们变得更加分裂、更加孤独，对未来的信心也比以往任何时候都低，尽管风险却在不断增加。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Robert Putnam.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与罗伯特·普特南的对话。

sentences.en: Dr. Putnam, your work is all about connection.
sentences.zh: 普特南博士，您的研究核心就是人际连接。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering first, can you describe your own social life?
sentences.zh: 所以首先我想问，您能描述一下您自己的社交生活吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what clubs are you in?
sentences.zh: 我是说，您参加了哪些俱乐部？

sentences.en: That's a really embarrassing question.
sentences.zh: 那真是一个令人尴尬的问题。

sentences.en: I write about and talk about the importance of connections, of social capital, which is my jargon for connections and trust and so on.
sentences.zh: 我撰写并探讨连接和“社会资本”的重要性，这是我用来指代连接、信任等概念的术语。

sentences.en: But my wife actually does it.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这些都是我妻子在做。

sentences.en: But she is actually the one who joins everything, who has been a tutor and a teacher and a terrific mother and an even better grandmother.
sentences.zh: 她才是那个加入各种组织的人，她当过导师、老师，是一位出色的母亲，更是一位了不起的祖母。

sentences.en: We've got two kids and seven grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 我们有两个孩子和七个孙辈。

sentences.en: And in the long run, her work is going to have a longer half-life than mine.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，她的工作所产生的影响力会比我的更持久。

sentences.en: I'm not just being modest because those kids are going to be around long after people have forgotten anything about this Putnam, the writer and author.
sentences.zh: 我这不是在谦虚，因为当人们早已忘记普特南这个作家时，那些孩子们依然会活跃在世上。

sentences.en: So that's a long way of saying not many clubs, am I right?
sentences.zh: 所以说了半天，意思就是没参加几个俱乐部，对吧？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When I was a kid, I joined everything.
sentences.zh: 我小时候什么都参加。

sentences.en: There's a picture of my high school yearbook, and basically there's nothing in my high school that I did not join.
sentences.zh: 我的高中毕业纪念册里有张照片，基本上我高中里没有任何活动是我没参加的。

sentences.en: Band and chorus and debate and even football and on and on.
sentences.zh: 乐队、合唱团、辩论队，甚至橄榄球队等等。

sentences.en: But as I've gotten older, I've gotten, it's hard to go to club meetings when you're on the road all the time.
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄增长，当你总是奔波在外时，很难去参加俱乐部会议。

sentences.en: And I am.
sentences.zh: 而我确实总是奔波在外。

sentences.en: That's the sad fact.
sentences.zh: 这就是残酷的事实。

sentences.en: That's interesting to me because you're grappling with, I think, something that we all grapple with, which is how harried our lives are,
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很有趣，因为我认为您正在处理我们所有人都在面对的问题，那就是我们的生活有多么匆忙，

sentences.en: how hard it is to actually find a meaningful connection.
sentences.zh: 找到真正有意义的连接有多么困难。

sentences.en: And a big part of why I was interested in having this conversation with you is that when it comes to social connection, things feel bad right now.
sentences.zh: 我之所以想和您进行这次对话，很大一部分原因在于，谈到社会连接时，现在的状况感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: Do things feel bad to you too?
sentences.zh: 您也觉得情况很糟糕吗？

sentences.en: Oh, sure.
sentences.zh: 哦，当然。

sentences.en: I think we're at a really important turning point in American history.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们正处于美国历史上一个非常重要的转折点。

sentences.en: Of course, American history is full of turning points, but this is a pretty important one.
sentences.zh: 当然，美国历史上充满了转折点，但这是一个相当重要的时刻。

sentences.en: What I wrote in Bowling Alone is even more relevant now.
sentences.zh: 我在《独自打保龄》中写的内容在今天甚至更具现实意义。

sentences.en: Now, why?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么呢？

sentences.en: Because what we've seen over the last 25 years since the book was published is a deepening and intensifying of that trend.
sentences.zh: 因为在书出版后的25年里，我们目睹了这一趋势的加深和加剧。

sentences.en: We become more socially isolated, and we can see it in every facet of our lives.
sentences.zh: 我们变得更加社会孤立，这一点在我们生活的方方面面都能看到。

sentences.en: We can see it in the Surgeon General's talk about loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我们可以从卫生局局长关于孤独的谈话中看到这一点。

sentences.en: And he's been talking about it relatively recently, and he's talking about the psychological state of being lonely.
sentences.zh: 他最近一直在谈论这个问题，他谈论的是孤独这种心理状态。

sentences.en: That's in Bowling Alone, the fact that people were becoming more and more socially isolated.
sentences.zh: 《独自打保龄》里就提到了人们正变得越来越社会孤立这一事实。

sentences.en: And the social isolation leads to lots of bad things.
sentences.zh: 而社会孤立会导致许多糟糕的后果。

sentences.en: We're seeing it right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就看到了。

sentences.en: Let me give you a particular example.
sentences.zh: 让我给您举个具体的例子。

sentences.en: Social isolation is really bad.
sentences.zh: 社会孤立真的很糟糕。

sentences.en: Well, it's bad for your health.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对你的健康有害。

sentences.en: That's part of the story of the book.
sentences.zh: 这是书中故事的一部分。

sentences.en: But it's really bad for the country because people who are isolated, and especially young men who are isolated, are vulnerable to the appeals of some false community.
sentences.zh: 但这对国家来说更糟糕，因为孤立的人，尤其是孤立的年轻男性，很容易受到虚假群体诉求的诱惑。

sentences.en: That was true, and I can cite chapter and verse on this.
sentences.zh: 这是事实，我可以对此引经据典。

sentences.en: Eager recruits to the Nazi Party in the 1930s were lonely, young German men.
sentences.zh: 20世纪30年代纳粹党的狂热新兵就是那些孤独的德国年轻男性。

sentences.en: And it's not an accident that the people who are most attractive today to white nationalist violence are lonely, young, white men.
sentences.zh: 今天，那些最容易被白人至上主义暴力所吸引的人是孤独的白人年轻男性，这绝非偶然。

sentences.en: Loneliness is bad for your health, but it's also bad for the health of the people around you.
sentences.zh: 孤独不仅对你的健康有害，对你周围人的健康也有害。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 说得通。

sentences.en: I want to understand a little bit about the terms that you use for how you describe this.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一下您用来描述这些情况的术语。

sentences.en: You distinguish between two types of social capital, right?
sentences.zh: 您区分了两种类型的社会资本，对吧？

sentences.en: There's bonding social capital, and there's bridging social capital.
sentences.zh: 一种是结合型社会资本，另一种是桥接型社会资本。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Can you explain that distinction?
sentences.zh: 您能解释一下这种区别吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Ties that link you to people like yourself
sentences.zh: 将你与同类人联系起来的纽带

sentences.en: are called bonding social capital.
sentences.zh: 被称为结合型社会资本。

sentences.en: That's just the way the word is used.
sentences.zh: 这个词就是这样用的。

sentences.en: So my ties to other elderly, male, white, Jewish professors,
sentences.zh: 所以，我与其他年长的、白人、犹太裔男性教授之间的纽带，

sentences.en: that's my bonding social capital.
sentences.zh: 那就是我的结合型社会资本。

sentences.en: And bridging social capital are your ties to people unlike yourself.
sentences.zh: 而桥接型社会资本是你与不同类人之间的纽带。

sentences.en: So my ties to people of a different generation or a different gender or a different religion or a different politics or whatever, that's my bridging social capital.
sentences.zh: 所以，我与不同代际、不同性别、不同宗教或不同政治立场的人之间的纽带，那就是我的桥接型社会资本。

sentences.en: I'm not saying bridging good, bonding bad, because if you get sick, the people who bring you chicken soup are likely to reflect your bonding social capital.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说桥接型就是好的，结合型就是坏的，因为如果你生病了，那些给你送鸡汤的人很可能就是你的结合型社会资本。

sentences.en: But I am saying that in a diverse society like ours, we need a lot of bridging social capital.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为，在我们这样一个多元化的社会中，我们需要大量的桥接型社会资本。

sentences.en: And some forms of bonding social capital are really awful.
sentences.zh: 而且某些形式的结合型社会资本确实非常可怕。

sentences.en: So the KKK is pure social capital.
sentences.zh: 比如三K党就是纯粹的社会资本。

sentences.en: Bonding social capital can be very useful, but it can also be extremely dangerous.
sentences.zh: 结合型社会资本可能非常有用，但也可能极其危险。

sentences.en: So far, so good.
sentences.zh: 目前为止，一切都好。

sentences.en: And except that bridging social capital is harder to build than bonding social capital.
sentences.zh: 除了桥接型社会资本比结合型社会资本更难建立之外。

sentences.en: But basically, that's the challenge, as I see it, of America today.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，这就是我所看到的当今美国的挑战。

sentences.en: There's a lot more to say about it, but the basic challenge is we need a lot more bridging social capital, and that's hard to do.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点还有很多可说的，但基本的挑战是我们急需更多的桥接型社会资本，而这很难做到。

sentences.en: And that's especially true in politics.
sentences.zh: 在政治领域尤其如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We'll get to politics, but I actually want to start by talking about individual connections.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会谈到政治，但我其实想先从个人连接谈起。

sentences.en: You know, in preparation for this interview, I talked to a lot of people about social isolation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，为了准备这次采访，我和很多人聊过社会孤立的问题。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: My 33-year-old niece feels it.
sentences.zh: 我33岁的侄女感受到了。

sentences.en: My nearly 60-year-old sister feels it.
sentences.zh: 我快60岁的姐姐也感受到了。

sentences.en: I feel it.
sentences.zh: 我也感受到了。

sentences.en: People think that they've lost the ability to connect.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他们已经失去了建立连接的能力。

sentences.en: 24 years ago, you placed a lot of blame on television.
sentences.zh: 24年前，您把很多责任归咎于电视。

sentences.en: Nowadays, many people place the blame on phones,
sentences.zh: 如今，许多人把责任归咎于手机，

sentences.en: although maybe that's too simplistic.
sentences.zh: 尽管这可能太简单化了。

sentences.en: Well, let me go back originally.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我回到最初。

sentences.en: At the time I wrote Bowling Alone,
sentences.zh: 在我写《独自打保龄》的时候，

sentences.en: social media was still six or seven years in the future.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体还要六七年才会出现。

sentences.en: I did speculate a little bit about social media, because I didn't guess that, but about the Internet.
sentences.zh: 我确实对社交媒体做了一些推测，因为我当时没猜到，但我推测了互联网的影响。

sentences.en: I did speculate a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我确实做了一些推测。

sentences.en: And as it happens, my speculations about the effects of the Internet turned out to be approximately right.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，我对互联网影响的推测大致是正确的。

sentences.en: And it's now a quite common idea that social media are to blame for all of our troubles.
sentences.zh: 现在，社交媒体应为我们所有的麻烦负责，这已经是一个非常普遍的观点了。

sentences.en: And I think that's a lot true.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在很大程度上是真的。

sentences.en: Although, even now, I don't think we should exculpate television.
sentences.zh: 尽管即使在今天，我也不认为我们应该为电视开脱。

sentences.en: There was a recent Nielsen report which said that, on average, the typical adult spends more than 10 hours each day with media.
sentences.zh: 最近有一份尼尔森报告显示，平均而言，典型的成年人每天花在媒体上的时间超过10小时。

sentences.en: Okay, 10 hours every day.
sentences.zh: 好吧，每天10小时。

sentences.en: Think of that.
sentences.zh: 想想看。

sentences.en: But about half of that is still devoted to television.
sentences.zh: 但其中大约一半的时间仍然花在电视上。

sentences.en: So even now, even long after the invention of the Internet and social media and the iPhone and so on, television still has that effect of privatizing our leisure time.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在今天，在互联网、社交媒体和iPhone等发明很久之后，电视仍然具有将我们的闲暇时间私有化的效果。

sentences.en: That's the fundamental thing it does.
sentences.zh: 这是它最根本的作用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're not interacting face-to-face with a real person.
sentences.zh: 我们没有与真实的人进行面对面的互动。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And one really important question that I don't think we really know is what is it about face-to-faceness that matters so much?
sentences.zh: 有一个非常重要的问题，我觉得我们还不太清楚，那就是“面对面”到底为什么如此重要？

sentences.en: Face-to-faceness matters.
sentences.zh: 面对面确实很重要。

sentences.en: There's no doubt about that.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And why it matters, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 至于为什么重要，我不知道。

sentences.en: Nobody knows.
sentences.zh: 没人知道。

sentences.en: But I want to add one more thing because to have that as a dichotomy, which most discussions of this have, is it better to do Facebook or better to go bowling on a team,
sentences.zh: 但我还想补充一点，因为如果把这个问题二元对立化，就像大多数讨论中所做的那样——是玩Facebook更好，还是去参加保龄球队更好，

sentences.en: that kind of issue, that is not the right way to think about the problem.
sentences.zh: 那种问题，并不是思考这个问题的正确方式。

sentences.en: What is?
sentences.zh: 那什么才是？

sentences.en: I want to use an analogy here with the concept of alloy.
sentences.zh: 我想在这里用“合金”的概念做一个类比。

sentences.en: An alloy is a mixture of two different metals, but mixing them together has unique characteristics.
sentences.zh: 合金是两种不同金属的混合物，但将它们混合在一起具有独特的特性。

sentences.en: Today, almost all of our social connections are simultaneously face-to-face and virtual.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们几乎所有的社会连接都是同时面对面和虚拟的。

sentences.en: Our social ties are all alloys.
sentences.zh: 我们的社会纽带都是“合金”。

sentences.en: Sometimes, my wife and I, for example, we have offices, you know, just next door, but often we send emails to each other.
sentences.zh: 有时，比如我和我妻子，我们有办公室，你知道，就在隔壁，但我们经常互发电子邮件。

sentences.en: How weird is that?
sentences.zh: 这有多奇怪？

sentences.en: I text my husband all the time, even if we're in the same house.
sentences.zh: 我经常给我丈夫发短信，即使我们就在同一个房子里。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Well, it turns out that's not peculiar to your marriage or my marriage.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，这并不是你或我的婚姻所特有的。

sentences.en: That's extremely common that our most intensive personal face-to-face ties are also the people with whom we interact virtually most of the time.
sentences.zh: 我们最紧密的个人面对面关系，往往也是我们大部分时间进行虚拟互动的人，这非常普遍。

sentences.en: So, there are ways in which we could combine face-to-face and internet that would be really productive.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们其实可以通过一些方式将面对面交流与互联网结合起来，从而产生非常积极的效果。

sentences.en: We could develop social media in a way that they would actually contribute to our lives, our personal lives, and our collective lives,
